SkyByrd Intake Sheet

SkyByrd Photography · website round two

What we need from you, Shawna

The mockups are built and they work — but 78 details in them are our best guess rather than your actual business. This sheet lists every one, grouped by how long it takes to answer. Print it and write on it, or reply to any of it by email; either is fine.

How to use this

Start at the top — the groups are ordered by how much they unblock. Pricing first, because every figure currently on the page was invented and it is the first thing your visitors will look for.

You do not need to answer everything before we go further. The first three groups alone would make the mockups honest enough to show anyone.

Contact details, your business name, your tagline and your service positioning are already correct — we verified those, and they are not in this list.

07

Your favourite places to shoot

Needs a think 1 item

Named places are more persuasive than adjectives — they help people picture their own session, and they bring in searches nobody else is competing for. Four to six real ones is plenty.

Locations

All six invented. Replace them with the places you genuinely use and love.

locations

We currently show

  1. The DuPage RiverWater, long grass and a low sun. Best in the hour before sunset.
  2. Downtown PlainfieldBrick, storefronts and shade. Good for branding and seniors who want an urban feel.
  3. Lake Renwick PreserveOpen prairie and big sky. Room for dogs to be dogs.
  4. Settlers’ ParkOld trees and wide paths. Easy with strollers and grandparents.
  5. The studioControlled light, no weather, no wind. Best for headshots and newborns.
  6. Your own homeThe rooms you actually live in. Quietly the most sentimental option.

08

How a session goes

Just check it 1 item

Drafted from your own descriptions in the earlier round. This was the best writing in the whole set, so we kept it — but check the timings are right.

Process

Steps 03 and 04 survive from concept 08 and are the strongest writing in the set. Confirm the response time and delivery window are accurate.

process

We currently show

  1. You send a dateNo payment, no forms. Just a note about who’s coming and roughly when. I reply within a day.
  2. We talk it throughTen minutes on the phone. Location, what to wear, how to handle the toddler who won’t sit still.
  3. The first ten minutes are throwawaysOn purpose. Everyone arrives stiff. I keep shooting anyway and it wears off faster than you’d think.
  4. Mostly walking, very little posingI’ll put you somewhere with good light and then largely get out of the way. No forced smiles.
  5. Your gallery, two weeks laterA private link that’s yours to keep. Order prints straight from it, or don’t — the files are the point.

Correct or confirm

09

Common questions

Just check it 1 item

Ten questions drafted from what people usually ask. This block quietly does more work than any other: it removes the hesitation that stops bookings, and it is what Google and AI assistants quote back to people. Correct any answer that is not how you actually work.

Faq

Ten questions drafted from common enquiries. Every answer needs your confirmation — particularly the rain policy, travel radius, deposit terms and delivery times.

faq

We currently show

  1. I’m not photogenic. Really.Nobody thinks they are — it is genuinely the most common thing people say to me. That is why the first ten minutes are throwaway frames and why we spend them talking. You will forget the camera is there sooner than you expect.
  2. What should we wear?I send a short guide once you book, with examples. The short version: coordinate rather than match, avoid big logos, and wear something you would actually choose. I am happy to look at photos of the options beforehand.
  3. How long does a session take?Family sessions run about 90 minutes, seniors about two hours, pets around 45 minutes, and branding is a half day. None of it is spent standing still.
  4. What if the kids melt down?They will, briefly. It is fine, it is built into the time, and those frames are usually the keepers.
  5. What happens if it rains?We reschedule, at no cost. Overcast is actually lovely light, so I will only move a session for real weather.
  6. How far do you travel?Across the southwest suburbs as standard — Naperville, Joliet, Oswego, Shorewood and the towns between. Further is usually possible, just ask.
  7. Do I need to pay a deposit to enquire?No. Sending a date costs nothing and commits you to nothing. We only talk about payment once you have decided.
  8. How many photos do we get, and how soon?Forty or more edited images for a family session, in a private gallery within two weeks. Usually sooner.
  9. Can we include grandparents or extended family?Please do. Extended family sessions are some of my favourite work, and they are frequently the reason people book in the first place.
  10. Can we order prints, or just download the files?Both. Prints, albums and canvases can be ordered straight from your gallery, and you also get a print release to use the files anywhere you like.

Correct or confirm
